title: The cap, the mandate and re-registration
objectives: Explain what a cap protects and how to set one.
Explain the exit-load consequence of re-registering an existing SIP.
body_md:
Three mechanics decide whether a step-up survives its first few years.

## The cap

A maximum instalment beyond which the step-up stops rising. It converts an open-ended commitment into a bounded one, which is often what a nervous client needs before agreeing. Where the AMC allows a cap, set it at a level the client is confident about.

## The mandate

The bank mandate limit must cover the highest future instalment. If it does not, a debit fails, and three consecutive failures cancel a monthly SIP. Raise the mandate when the step-up is set up, not when it first fails.

## Re-registration

If the existing SIP has no step-up facility, converting may mean cancelling and registering a new SIP. That resets the instalment clock, so the newest units restart the exit-load period. Explain that before doing it, and consider a second smaller SIP instead.
example: A ₹10,000 SIP with a 10% step-up reaches ₹16,105 by year six. If the mandate is set at ₹15,000, the debit fails in year six — so the mandate is raised to ₹25,000 at the start.
say: We'll set a cap so the instalment stops at a level you're comfortable with.
Converting this SIP means re-registering it, which restarts the exit-load clock on new units.
never: The mandate can stay at today's amount.

check.q: A ₹10,000 SIP with a 10% step-up will reach about ₹16,105 by year six. The mandate is ₹15,000. What happens?
o: The debit fails, and consecutive failures can cancel the SIP
check.why: The mandate must cover the highest future instalment. Set it higher at the start.

check.q: What does re-registering an existing SIP do?
o: It resets the instalment clock, so new units restart the exit-load period
check.why: A new registration means new instalment dates and new exit-load clocks. Explain it before acting.

check.q: When a client is nervous about committing, what helps most?
o: A cap, plus the option to pause or reduce at review
check.why: A cap makes the commitment bounded, and a review date makes it revisitable.
